label: Identification in simultaneous equation models — mastery test

items.stem: A structural equation represents:
options: a behavioural relationship in the simultaneous system
a forecast equation with no disturbances
items.explanation: Structural coefficients describe the behavioural equations that jointly determine endogenous variables.

items.stem: A reduced-form equation expresses an endogenous variable as a function of:
options: all exogenous variables and a reduced-form disturbance
items.explanation: Solving the simultaneous system expresses endogenous variables in terms of exogenous variables and transformed disturbances.

items.stem: In a standard demand-supply system, market price is usually:
items.explanation: Price is jointly determined by demand and supply, so it responds to structural shocks in both equations.

items.stem: An equation has 1 endogenous RHS variable and 2 excluded exogenous variables. By order it is:
items.explanation: The excluded-variable count k=2 exceeds m=1, so it is overidentified by order.
items.check: Two excluded variables exceed one endogenous RHS variable.

items.stem: The order condition compares:
options: excluded exogenous variables with endogenous RHS variables
included exogenous variables with all endogenous variables
the number of equations with sample size
the number of instruments with observations
items.explanation: The order count is made equation by equation and uses exogenous variables excluded from that equation.

items.stem: The order condition is:
items.explanation: A rank-deficient cross-equation coefficient matrix can fail identification even when the order count passes.

items.stem: If an equation has k<m, it is:
items.explanation: Too few excluded exogenous variables fail the necessary order condition.

items.stem: If m=2 endogenous RHS variables and k=2 excluded exogenous variables, the order classification is:
items.explanation: The counts are equal, so it is exactly identified by order; rank still needs checking.
items.check: Equality is only the order classification, not proof that rank holds.

items.stem: The rank condition is concerned with:
options: linear independence in the relevant cross-equation coefficients
whether all structural disturbances are normal
the magnitude of R² in the reduced form
items.explanation: Rank asks whether the excluded exogenous variables provide enough independent identifying variation.

items.stem: Two excluded variables have proportional coefficient columns. Their column rank is:
options: equal to the number of observations
items.explanation: Proportional nonzero columns span one direction, so their rank is one.

items.stem: For the matrix [[2,4],[1,2]], the rank is:
items.explanation: The second column is twice the first; only one independent column remains.
items.check: The determinant is zero and one column is a multiple of the other.

items.stem: An equation with k>m and a full rank condition is:
items.explanation: More excluded exogenous variables than endogenous RHS variables create overidentifying restrictions when rank holds.

items.stem: In the demand equation Q=α₀+α₁P+α₂Y+u, if P is endogenous and W is excluded, W can identify demand when:
options: W shifts supply and the relevant rank coefficient is nonzero
W is correlated with the demand disturbance
W has no effect anywhere in the system
items.explanation: The excluded supply shifter must create independent variation in equilibrium price without entering demand directly.

items.stem: Which statements about the identification conditions are correct? A. The order condition is a count. B. The order condition is sufficient. C. The rank condition checks independent variation. D. If k<m, the equation is overidentified.
items.explanation: A and C are true. The order condition is only necessary; if k<m the equation is underidentified, and rank must still be checked when the count passes.
statements: The order condition is a count
The rank condition checks independent variation
If k<m, the equation is overidentified

A.why: The order condition is the necessary count of excluded exogenous variables.

B.why: A passing count is not sufficient; the rank condition can still fail.

C.why: The rank condition requires enough independent cross-equation coefficients.

D.why: If k<m, the equation is underidentified, not overidentified.

items.stem: If k=m and rank holds, the equation is:
items.explanation: Equal counts with the required rank identify the equation exactly.

items.stem: Demand is Q=10−2P+3Y+u_d; supply is Q=2+P+4W+u_s. The denominator when solving for P is:
items.explanation: Equating demand and supply gives 10−2P+3Y+u_d=2+P+4W+u_s, so 3P is isolated.
items.check: Collecting −2P−P on one side gives a coefficient magnitude of 3.

items.stem: For the same system, the reduced-form coefficient of W in P is:
items.explanation: Equilibrium gives 3P=8+3Y−4W+u_d−u_s, so the coefficient on W is −4/3.

items.stem: For an equation with two endogenous right-hand-side variables, which statements are correct? A. Two excluded variables satisfy the order count. B. Two proportional columns have rank two. C. Full rank two is required. D. The order condition alone proves identification.
items.explanation: A and C are true. Two excluded variables meet the order count, but proportional columns have rank one and the order condition alone is insufficient.
statements: Two excluded variables satisfy the order count
Two proportional columns have rank two
The order condition alone proves identification

A.why: The order condition is the necessary count of excluded exogenous variables.

B.why: A passing count is not sufficient; the rank condition can still fail.

C.why: The rank condition requires enough independent cross-equation coefficients.

D.why: If k<m, the equation is underidentified, not overidentified.

items.stem: If the order condition passes but the rank condition fails, the equation is:
items.explanation: The rank condition is decisive: deficient rank means the required independent identifying variation is absent.

items.stem: In the demand-supply example, the reduced-form coefficient on Y in P is:
items.explanation: From 3P=8+3Y−4W+u_d−u_s, dividing by 3 gives coefficient 1 on Y.
